description: We’re Romi and Ofir, siblings with backgrounds in Marine Biotechnology and Data Engineering. Our skills include research, statistics, Python, SQL, and machine learning. We’re curious and collaborative, looking for teammates with coding, AI/ML, or design skills to build something useful together.
summary: Planetary Analogs is an interactive atlas that addresses NASA’s challenge by finding Earth analogs for specific mission tests. We combine datasets from multiple sources across more than 20,000 Earth locations and let researchers decide what kind of similarity matters. For the same target on Mars, the atlas can surface one set of sites for testing rover mobility and another for testing a rock sampling instrument. This approach brings overlooked locations into consideration and shows which features drove each match and where conditions differ, giving researchers a shortlist they can validate in the field.
details:
Planetary Analogs helps mission teams find places on Earth to test robots and instruments for the Moon and Mars.* The best analog depends on the experiment. A rover mobility trial calls for similar slopes and roughness. A trial of an instrument that analyzes soil calls for similar relative chemical composition. Our explorer lets researchers choose the objective and see how it changes the shortlist.

We used GIS to link lunar and Martian mission records with elevation, measured chemistry and mapped geology across more than 20,000 Earth sites. The explorer compares terrain over windows of approximately 5 × 5 km and compares chemistry using ratios between measured components. It scales numerical differences by the spread of each feature across Earth sites, then combines the distances using weights for the selected experiment. Optional sunlight matching compares modeled daylight conditions at reference times. The explorer shows each candidate on a map, with its measured differences and source records available for inspection. Gemini explains the similarities and tradeoffs using the computed results.

The same planetary sample can produce different recommendations for different experiments. For Apollo 17 sample *78221,71, Austria ranks first in the terrain-only comparison, while Japan ranks first in the geochemistry-oriented comparison. Combining NASA mission records, Copernicus elevation and open national geological surveys also makes it possible to surface candidates beyond familiar analog sites. We used Canadian Space Agency RADARSAT-1 archive data to add radar context for 15 surveyed sites in Tasmania.

The project helps teams narrow a broad search to sites worth investigating and see what still needs field verification. We considered measurement availability, differences in spatial scale, and traceability to the original sources. We built the data pipeline with Python, GIS tools and SQLite, the explorer with HTML, CSS, JavaScript and Leaflet, and the explanation feature with the Gemini API. The public demo runs on Render.
